params._roi_note: start_y RE-CENTRED 684 -> 692 for PAR-5. PAR-4 parked at y +5.95 px, and the 20x20 tracking window centres on the beam and spans +-10 px, so it reached 15.95 px against the 32x32 ROI's 15.5 px half-width -- the window ran off the edge, truncating the spot and desensitizing the centroid by roughly 2x. That is why PAR-4's y rejection fell by almost exactly half in EVERY low band (1-10 Hz 4.8->2.4x, 10-30 15.8->7.7x, 30-60 9.8->6.0x): a uniform loss of rejection across the band is the signature of a loop-gain error, not of environment or of incomplete convergence. Park VERIFIED before this run at y +0.70 px / x +0.53 px over 13 s, the best centring of any PAR run. RULE: measure the park position before every run and re-derive the ROI once |park| > ~2 px; the beam walks several px per hour, which is also the likeliest explanation for the Kx sweeps reading 3.97-4.36 across one morning.
params._exposure: 50, matching conf_bode_par_x/y.json and steering_tuned.json. This is not cosmetic: exposure smear is part of the loop delay (about exposure/2, i.e. 0.19 frame at 50 us against 0.95 frame at 250 us), and the delay configured in the fsp block was fit through a chain running at 50. Going back to 250 adds ~0.4 frame the fit does not know about. Re-bode if you want the longer exposure.

params._threshold: 5 as of 2026-07-30: the camera is now shrouded and the background floor is low, so the high threshold that used to be needed to reject stray light costs signal for nothing. Matches conf_bode_par_x/y.json and steering_par_fsp.json.

pipeline._watcher_units: RUN watch_error_ts.jl WITH -p 32. Its default is pixel=64 (watch_error_ts.jl:52), which sets PIX_PER_UNIT=(64-1)/2=31.5 against the correct (32-1)/2=15.5 for this ROI -- so the live readout is 2.03x HIGH unless -p 32 is passed. Its --com std is also CUMULATIVE from process start, so a watcher left running through the open phase reports a figure dominated by open-loop motion, not the closed phase. attenuation_test's pixel_scale 15.5 is the correct one.

pipeline._note: Full-rate [y,x] ERROR record, BEFORE fsp -- the measured error, not the command. Two reasons it is here from PAR-3 on: (1) attenuation_test buffers the open phase in RAM and only writes its .dat/PDF at ATTEN_PHASE_DONE (attenuation_test.c:617 frees the buffers on fini without flushing), so any abort throws the whole 500 s open measurement away -- this file makes a partial run recoverable. (2) It is an independent check on the reported RMS: the time-domain std of the closed segment must reproduce the '# stat' line in the .dat once scaled by 15.5 px/unit. ~260 MB for the 1220 s run.

pipeline._note1: THE TEST. Sits after the CoM sinks (watchers see the true error) and before the FSP. pass_open=FALSE here: the open phase feeds the FSP zeros, so it starts the closed phase with zero weights and learns live (see the _pass_open note). Either way the DAC parks at 0 V for the whole open phase and the recorded open PSD is identical -- only fsp's internal view of the error changes. settle_time covers FSP/NLMS/adapt re-convergence after closure. pixel_scale 15.5 = (32-1)/2 for the 32x32 ROI. 500/500 @ nfft 4096 matches attenuation_fsp15/21 for a SHARED frequency grid -> directly comparable closed RMS.

params._settle_time: 600, RAISED from 120 on 2026-07-30. Run 3's error record showed the closed-loop residual still falling 500 s after closure: exponential fits give asymptote 0.0404 px with tau 255 s (y) and 0.0855 px with tau 125 s (x), against 500 s window averages of 0.0565 and 0.0891. The open phase was flat to slightly WORSENING over the same period, so this is the observer converging, not the environment calming. tau is 30-60x the nominal NLMS constant order/(mu*fs) = 4.5 s -- the classic LMS result that the weakest eigenmodes converge in proportion to the eigenvalue spread of the input, and this disturbance spectrum spans ~4.4 decades. At 120 s the scored window was mostly transient and understated y by 40%. 600 s is ~2.4 tau on y. Total run is now 100+500+600+500 = 1700 s.
params._pass_open: FALSE for this first par run: the open phase feeds fsp zeros, so the FIR never sees open-loop data and starts the closed phase with zero weights, learning live -- the pre-2026-07-27 style. The open MEASUREMENT is unaffected: attenuation_test.c records the sample before zeroing the vector, so the open PSD is identical either way.
params.config:
ATTENUATION PAR-7 -- a REPEAT OF THE PAR-5 CONTROLLER. broad_lp is back to 5 and the timeline back to 100/500/600/500, so this file is once again PAR-5 exactly; only the output filenames are bumped to 7 so PAR-5 and PAR-6 data are not overwritten. WHY: PAR-6 tested broad_lp 9 and it is not worth keeping (see _broad_lp -- it buys 100-150 Hz +82% and 250-400 Hz +48% on x but pays -41% x / -19% y at 1-30 Hz, netting y -2% / x +10%).
PAR-6 ALSO NEEDS AN ASTERISK, and this is the reason a clean repeat is wanted: someone leaned on the mount TWICE during it. A burst at t~270 s inside the open phase, and -- worse -- a cluster of spikes at t=1668-1690 s INSIDE the 1200-1700 s scored closed window, 1 s RMS reaching y 0.250 / x 0.258 against a 0.041 / 0.086 baseline. That tail alone moves the scored y from 0.0430 to 0.0566 px (+32%) and x from 0.0894 to 0.0941 (+5%), and the first reading of PAR-6 as a large y regression was entirely an artefact of it. All PAR-6 numbers quoted here are from windows trimmed to open 110-265 + 285-595 and closed 1200-1670. KEEP PEOPLE OFF THE TABLE FOR THE FULL 28 MINUTES, and check atten_par_err7.aylp for bumps before trusting any result.
PAR-6 environment for reference: its own open, with the bump excised, was y 0.5104 / x 0.3777 px, genuinely 9%/19% above the PAR-3 reference open (y 0.4685 / x 0.3162) that PAR-5 was scored against -- so the environment does move between runs and the WITHIN-RUN ratio is the number to trust whenever the open phase is clean. Everything from here down describes PAR-5 and still applies. PAR-5 was: PAR-4 REPEATED with the beam RE-CENTRED (start_y 684 -> 692, park verified +0.70 px y / +0.53 px x, against PAR-4's +5.95 px which ran the 20x20 tracking window off the ROI edge and halved y's rejection in every band) and with the NLMS step SCHEDULED 0.5 -> 0.03 over 60 s to fix the convergence PAR-4's trace showed was still incomplete. Kx stays 4.05 -- PAR-4 proved it: x improved in every band (60-150 Hz 1.4x -> 2.9x, 150-250 Hz from 0.4x amplifying to 1.3x rejecting) and beat its environment-scaled predicted asymptote by 11%. Timeline unchanged from PAR-4 so the scored windows are directly comparable. Through the PARPORT DAC (TI DAC81404 over the StarTech PEX1P2 / AX99100 PCIe parallel card, spi link, mmio backend), replacing the DAQC2/BRIDGEplate serial path used by every previous attenuation run.
TRANSPORT: bit-banged 24-bit SPI, ~6.4 us per channel update (~12.8 us for both channels), against the BRIDGEplate's ~0.5-1.4 ms. DAC range is FIXED at +-5 V bipolar (153 uV/LSB) with the mirror parked at 0 V, matching the bode sweeps exactly; auto-ranging is off, so the actuator is a fixed-gain element for both phases of the A/B and the open/closed comparison is clean. Supplies +/-12 V: AVDD needs VMAX+1.5 = 11.5 V for +-10, AVSS -11.5 V, leaving only 0.5 V of margin -- meter the rails under load. AVSS is therefore NEGATIVE, not grounded, which means the 0-5 base range runs outside the AVSS = 0 V condition SLASEH2A 7.5 gives the unipolar figures at (see _avss_tradeoff); 16-bit = 76 uV/LSB in 0-5, 305 uV/LSB in +-10, vs the BRIDGEplate's 12-bit 1 mV.
OUTPUTS: two channels, no coarse stage -- ch0 = y/tip (+1.0 V/unit), ch1 = x/tilt (-1.0 V/unit), offset 0 V, symmetric command bounds +-1 V (59 px of authority against a +-16 px ROI; the mirror's full range is deliberately NOT given to the loop on this first run). NOTE the command->FSM voltage mapping is NOT the same as any previous attenuation run, so K is not comparable across the transport change and was re-measured -- and it came out 4.7-5.5x HIGHER, not lower as this file originally predicted, so nothing about the piplate-era gains carries over.
Camera/CoM: 32x32 ROI start_x 1832 / start_y 662 (re-derived 2026-07-31 immediately before PAR-6; park measured 4x at exposures 50/50/20/10 reading x 1846.2/1845.7/1846.2/1846.0 and y 677.2/677.1/677.2/676.8, std 0.24/0.19 px, giving a beam offset of -1.3 px x / -0.3 px y from frame centre and 4.7 px of tracking-window clearance -- against the 1.0 px clearance that a +5 px park had left earlier the same day, and PAR-4's edge-clipping park), exposure 50, gain 100, bw 100, 20x20 tracked window thr 5 (the camera is now shrouded, so the background floor no longer needs a high threshold). Identical to conf_bode_par_x/y[_small].json, so K and tau were fit through exactly this optical chain.
FSP: broad_order 512, broad_mu .03 -- REVERTED from PAR-2's 128/.005, which was 60% worse on y and 10% on x once normalised for the environment. 128 taps = 29.6 Hz resolution cannot separate the 2-3 Hz-spaced 9-30 Hz comb; this reproduces the documented kalman order-80 failure (order 80 ~29 Hz could not represent the 2.256 Hz comb). broad_lp 5 -- PAR-6 tried 9 and it was reverted (see _broad_lp for the full result; 5 covers the 685 Hz delay ring it was chosen for, and although it gives only -2.0 dB at the 280 Hz command-noise hump that carries 90% of x's closed variance, buying that stopband costs prediction horizon and the horizon is worth more); adapt_period 8, adapt_tau 5. Guard ON (guard_ratio 4). Cold-start observer: pass_open false + broad_freeze_closed false, so no weight is derived from open-loop data; drift_tau and the transient path are OFF. Modal freqs re-derived from run 1's own open PSD (8-mode cap), though they are inert while broad_order > 0.
PURPOSE: isolate the two things PAR-4 confounded. PAR-4 changed Kx AND happened to run with the beam 5.95 px off centre; x improved everywhere (the Kx fix) while y lost half its rejection uniformly across 1-60 Hz (the clipped tracking window). PAR-5 fixes the centring and changes nothing else about the controller except the step schedule, which the offline replay shows does not move the converged solution. EXPECTATIONS: y should return to a closed/open ratio near PAR-3's 0.121 (PAR-4 was 0.233); x should hold or beat PAR-4's 0.248 (PAR-3 was 0.302). Prior absolute numbers are NOT directly comparable because the environment moves run to run -- PAR-4's open was 18% (y) and 34% (x) larger than PAR-3's, and a new 150-250 Hz component appeared that carried 8.7x (y) and 5x (x) more open power than in PAR-3. Always normalise the closed RMS by that run's own open RMS before claiming an improvement.
DELAY AND K: taken from different sweeps on purpose. DELAY from the newest full 5-300 Hz sweeps, fsm_bodex_par2 / fsm_bodey_par2 (2026-07-31 12:23 / 12:16): x 2.763 fr (tau 0.4654 ms), y 2.624 fr (tau 0.4288 ms) at fs 3788. PAR-1..3 ran 2.717 / 2.577; the +0.046 fr shift sits inside the fits' own phase residuals, so the two sweep pairs agree and the newer/longer value is kept only because under-modeled delay is the documented failure mode. K from the SMALL-SIGNAL plateau: Kx 4.05, Ky 3.646. That distinction is not academic -- the loop commands ~6 mV rms / ~20 mV peak and the FSM compresses ~4% at +-100 mV, but WHICH AXIS compresses moves between days: on 07-30 it was x (100/50 mV ratio 1.041, y flat at 0.998), on 07-31 it was y (ratio 1.039, x flat at 1.003). The raw 07-31 fit lines therefore read Kx 4.050 (correct) and Ky 3.510 (3.7% low), and PAR-4 uses 3.646 for y from the +-20 mV sweep, corroborated by the same full file's +-50 mV pass at 3.662. Conversely tau is NOT measurable from a small sweep -- 10-30 Hz spans ~7 deg of phase and their loop_frames scatters 1.09-2.02 fr -- which is why delay comes only from the full sweeps. Against the piplate era this is ~5x MORE loop gain and LESS THAN HALF the delay; the shorter delay is the entire reason to expect better rejection here. Caveat: the small-signal gain itself wanders a few percent per hour (seven +-20 mV x sweeps read 3.97-4.36, each internally consistent), and erring HIGH on K is the safe direction since u = -phi_hat/K.
COMPARE against attenuation_fsp21 and attenuation_fsp15 (run 15: y 0.073 / x 0.168 px): report total and per-band closed RMS, 60-400 Hz waterbed, command/clamp behavior, and transient activation count on the shared 500/500/4096 grid. Closed RMS in PIXELS remains comparable across the change; command units do not. refs: Kulcsar 2006 / Petit 2008 / Meimon 2010 / Correia 2010

pipeline._K_warning:
K IS THE SMALL-SIGNAL PLATEAU, never the raw fit line of a +-100 mV sweep. PAR-4 runs Kx 4.05 / Ky 3.646 against PAR-1..3's 3.787 / 3.636 -- the Kx move is the one controller change here. The loop commands ~6 mV rms / ~20 mV peak; a +-100 mV sweep drives an order of magnitude harder and the FSM compresses ~4% there.
Evidence, per axis, per amplitude (<=30 Hz plateau):
  x 07-30: 100 mV 3.815 / 50 mV 3.971 (ratio 1.041)  -- compressing
  x 07-31: 100 mV 4.050 / 50 mV 4.092 / 20 mV 4.056 / 8 mV 4.020 (ratio 1.003) -- flat
  y 07-30: 100 mV 3.664 / 50 mV 3.655 (ratio 0.998)  -- flat
  y 07-31: 100 mV 3.523 / 50 mV 3.662 / 20 mV 3.646 / 8 mV 3.668 (ratio 1.039) -- compressing
So compression is real but SWAPS AXES between days: the raw 07-31 fit lines read Kx 4.050 (right) and Ky 3.510 (3.7% low, would have under-modeled y). Always run the small sweep, or at minimum read the half-amplitude second pass of the full one.
WHY IT MATTERS FOR PAR-4: since u = -phi_hat/K, PAR-1..3's Kx 3.787 against a true ~4.05 was a ~7% OVER-command on x and nothing on y -- exactly the asymmetry PAR-3 reported (x disturbance 28% above the open-phase error, x closed-window bound above the open-window one, y clean). y is the control: if PAR-4 improves x and leaves y alone, that is the K fix and not the environment.
CAVEAT: the small-signal gain itself wanders a few percent over an hour. Seven +-20 mV x sweeps read 4.08, 3.97, 4.35, 4.35, 4.36, 4.07, 4.06, each file internally consistent across both of its passes, so it is the plant/beam moving, not noise; y drifted 3.706 -> 3.695 -> 3.645 -> 3.646 the same morning. 4.05 is x's most recent value from BOTH the full and small sweeps. If PAR-4 shows guard trips or ~690 Hz command activity, move x UP toward the 4.19 seven-run mean, never below 4.05. In physical units 4.05 = 62.8 px/V = 15.9 mV/px. Re-measure after any re-centre, ROI change or exposure change.
pipeline._note2: K is the SIGNED command->error gain (error units per command unit). Its SIGN (y +, x -) belongs to the optical/mechanical path and carries over; only the magnitude is invalid. K is also bias-dependent.
pipeline._note3: With broad_order>0 the identified full-band observer supplies the command and the AR2 modal estimate is not added, avoiding double cancellation.
pipeline._note4: zeta ~0.002 = sharp line; ~0.3 = broadband hump. adapt_period>0 turns on Petit/Meimon re-identification every 8 s.

PAR-1..3 ran 2.717 / 2.577 from the 07-30 sweeps; the +0.046 / +0.047 fr shift is ~1.3 deg at 300 Hz against 1.71 / 2.69 deg phase residuals, so the two independent sweeps agree and this is a re-confirmation. params._fs: 3788 inherited from the piplate era. The camera should still be the bottleneck, but the DAC no longer adds to the loop period -- confirm the achieved rate and update fs (and the bode_par sample_rate) if it has moved, since delay in FRAMES depends on it.
params._broad_order: RUN 2 CHANGE, and the only one that can move the number: 512/0.03 -> 128/0.005, the attenuation12 operating point. doc/devices/fsp.md states outright that 'attenuation11 showed that 512 taps at 0.03 preserved more high-frequency coefficient noise than the additional prediction accuracy justified' -- and run 1 used the superseded attenuation11 setting. That HF coefficient noise is the leading suspect for run 1's two weak spots: only 1.5x rejection over 60-150 Hz (now the largest closed contributor on both axes) and a 3.4-3.5x waterbed at 195-250 Hz. Cost is convergence time: order/(mu*fs) goes 4.5 s -> 6.8 s, still ~18 time constants inside the 120 s settle. Rollback: 512 / 0.03.
params._broad_mu_init:
NEW for PAR-5, the convergence fix. PAR-4's trace showed the FIR still growing 20.7% (x) and 7.5% (y) THROUGH the scored window, i.e. 600 s of settle was still not enough and the run scored a controller that had not stopped moving. Cause is the classic LMS one: convergence per eigenmode is proportional to that mode's eigenvalue, and this disturbance spans ~4.4 decades, so the nominal constant order/(mu*fs) = 4.5 s becomes a measured 125-255 s. A single mu cannot fix it -- large converges fast but leaves a mu/(2-mu) misadjustment floor, small is quiet but slow -- so the step is now SCHEDULED: 0.5 at loop close decaying to 0.03 with a 60 s constant. Verified by replaying PAR-4's own open-phase record through the same 512-tap NLMS: prediction error at t=20 s is 0.062 px scheduled against 0.220 px constant (3.6x), at t=100 s 0.086 vs 0.139, and by t>=300 s the two are IDENTICAL to within noise. That last point is what makes it safe here: mu affects the path and the steady-state misadjustment, not the optimum, and mu is back to 0.03 by t=900 s -- 300 s before the scored window opens at 1200 s. The timeline is deliberately unchanged from PAR-4 (100/500/600/500) so the scored windows stay directly comparable; if the trace confirms early convergence, settle_time can be cut in PAR-6.
WHICH RUNS USED WHAT: PAR-1..PAR-4 ran a CONSTANT broad_mu 0.03; PAR-5 (2026-07-31) was the first with this schedule (0.5 -> 0.03, tau 60) and is the current reference -- best y on record. So the schedule stays ON by default: it is what PAR-5 and everything after it use. Set broad_mu_init to 0 ONLY to reproduce PAR-1..PAR-4, never merely 'to be safe' -- matching PAR-5 means leaving it on.
MEASURED COST on PAR-5: the schedule leaves the filter LARGER (||w|| 1.95 vs PAR-4's 0.92) and a larger filter injects more HF command noise. PAR-5's x paid for it at 250-400 Hz (0.0169 -> 0.0475 px, 2.8x worse), which cancelled x's 59-71% gain below 30 Hz; y gained 33% net. So it is not a pure path-only change -- it moves the endpoint, which is exactly why the setting has to match across any two runs being compared.
params._broad_lp:
5 taps. REVERTED 2026-07-31 from the 9 that PAR-6 tested. KEEP IT AT 5 unless you are deliberately re-opening this. What 9 was for: PAR-5's converged x predictor ran mean |W| 1.03 across 200-350 Hz against y's 0.44 (||w|| 0.915 vs 0.417), i.e. near-unity observer gain on content that is pure sensor floor (x's OPEN loop above 100 Hz is only 0.021 px), so it was identifying its own command echo and injecting broadband noise -- x's Bode integral int ln|S| df was +847 against y's -46, positive in every band above 100 Hz. 9 taps give -7.6 dB at 280 Hz against 5's -2.0 dB.
PAR-6 RESULT, on windows cleaned of two mount bumps (see the config note): it WORKS where it was aimed and LOSES more elsewhere. Rejection x 100-150 Hz +82%, 250-400 Hz +48%; but 1-30 Hz x -41% / y -19%, and 1-30 Hz is where nearly all the power is. Net total rejection y -2%, x +10% -- not worth the complexity. The mechanism of the loss is NOT mysterious: broad_gd goes (9-1)/2 = 4 frames against 5's 2, and that lands directly in the prediction horizon (bd = delay + broad_gd), 4.76 -> 6.76 frames.
DO NOT TRY TO ESCAPE THAT WITH A CLEVERER FILTER -- it was checked and the trade is fundamental. A minimum-phase version of the boxcar-9 magnitude has the IDENTICAL 4.00 frame passband group delay (the boxcar's zeros sit on the unit circle, so it is already the minimum-delay filter for its own magnitude), and Butterworth-shaped magnitudes trade at the same rate (2nd-order fc 200 Hz: gd 3.57 fr for -6.9 dB at 280, vs boxcar 9's 4.00 fr for -7.6 dB). Ridge/leakage on the NLMS update was also checked and does the WRONG thing: it shrinks the large low-frequency directions and leaves |W| at 200-400 Hz essentially untouched (0.423 -> 0.411 as the ridge goes 0 -> 3% of tr(R)/P), because in the CLOSED-loop input the HF is well-excited, not low-eigenvalue.
WHERE THE ACTUAL FIX LIVES, and why it costs no horizon: solve the Wiener predictor on PAR-5's OWN closed-loop spectrum and the optimum wants |W| = 0.42 across 200-400 Hz -- the live filter drifted to 1.03. The unity HF gain is therefore NOT what the statistics justify; it is a closed-loop equilibrium sustained by ongoing adaptation, the same failure mode already documented for kalman gain < 1. That means ~-7.8 dB is available at 200-400 Hz -- MORE than boxcar 9's -5.6 dB -- for free, by stopping the filter from drifting there: broad_freeze_closed true (it is false in this file), ideally with the weights identified on open-loop data via pass_open true or a wiener_file, and/or a lower per-axis broad_mu on x. Those are the next things to try, NOT a longer prefilter. Corroborating evidence that adaptation never settles: ||w|| reached y 3.512 / x 2.766 in PAR-6 against PAR-4's y 0.417 / x 0.915, with ||dw|| still nonzero at the end of the run.
params._wiener_out: NEW for PAR-4: dumps the LEARNED 512-tap y/x predictors at exit, in exactly the format wiener_file reads. This run is the first whose scored window is actually converged (settle_time 600 s), so its weights are the first worth keeping. Written from fini, which runs on the SIGINT path too, so a Ctrl-C at 1200 s still saves them. The header records broad_order/mu/lp, fs, per-axis horizon and K, the closed-frame count, and ||w|| per axis -- compare ||w|| against a later run to see whether the observer is settling or still growing. To REPLAY these weights, point wiener_file at this file, but only in a run with the same broad_order, horizon, broad_lp and drift_tau: taps mean nothing against a different model, and the loader's index check cannot catch a horizon mismatch. Pair it with broad_freeze_closed true to score a frozen predictor.
params._wiener_trace: THE ANSWER TO PAR-4's QUESTION, sampled every 5 s (340 lines over the 1700 s run, ~50 kB). settle_time was raised 120 -> 600 s on the strength of an exponential fit to PAR-3's error record; this measures the convergence directly instead of inferring it. ||dw|| is the tap change since the previous sample -- it flattening BEFORE t=1200 (when the scored closed window opens) is what makes 600 s defensible, and it still falling means 600 s is still not enough. Also a free correctness check on pass_open false: during the open phase fsp is fed zeros, the NLMS step is mu*pe/energy with energy floored at 1e-12, so pe = 0 gives EXACTLY zero weight change -- ||dw|| must be 0.0 for every sample before t=600, and any nonzero value there means open-loop data is leaking into the observer. Flushed per sample, so it survives an abort. Columns are in the file header.
params._broad_freeze_closed: FALSE for this first par run, matching steering_par_fsp.json: the FIR keeps adapting through the closed phase instead of applying a frozen set. With pass_open false as well, no weight in this run is derived from open-loop data -- the observer starts at zero and learns as it goes. NLMS time constant is order/(mu*fs) = 512/(0.03*3788) = 4.5 s, so the 120 s settle_time is ~27 time constants and the closed recording begins on a converged observer. The doc default is true because continuous closed-loop NLMS can learn leaked command as disturbance when K or the delay is mismodelled; the defence against that is broad_lp (now 9). Do NOT count the burst guard as the second defence on this transport: its band-pass is centred on fs/(2*(delay+delay_frac)) = ~685/722 Hz, an octave above the 280 Hz feature PAR-5 actually exhibited, so it sat through +18 dB of x regeneration without tripping. It is clear of the 316/344 Hz leakage that false-tripped it in the piplate era, but it is now also clear of the thing worth catching. Restore true for a frozen-observer comparison run.
params._two_timescale: BOTH HALVES OFF for this run, matching steering_par_fsp.json, which carries neither. drift_tau is simply not needed for a first number; the transient path had to go because it is INCOMPATIBLE with starting cold. Run 2026-07-30: it latched the instant the loop closed and would have held the whole 500 s closed phase in the u = -(drift_hat + 0.25*error)/K servo instead of predictive cancellation. Why: fsp.c:397 only updates the quiet-innovation variance while the transient path is INACTIVE, so with pass_open false feeding it zeros for the 600 s hold, transient_var converged to ~0 and the threshold fell back to transient_floor = 0.03. The FIR was also still at zero weights, so the residual at close was the raw error (0.021-0.028 rms, peaks well past 0.03) -- event true nearly every frame, fsp.c:394 resetting t_event, never the 0.10 s of quiet needed to recover. It is a deadlock, not a trip: while active the variance cannot update (threshold can never rise) AND NLMS/modal learning is frozen (the predictor can never train out of it). transient_floor 0.03 was sized for pass_open=true, where fsp learns sigma ~0.025 during the hold and the 6-sigma threshold lands near 0.15. If you want the transient path back on a cold start, set transient_floor above the open-loop error peaks (~0.15), do NOT rely on the 6-sigma term.
params._drift_tau_rollback: 2.0 if you want the slow-drift EWMA split back; it was not implicated in the 07-30 latch.
params._clamp_why_here: These are fsp's OWN bounds, deliberately not a downstream anyloop:clamp stage. fsp applies the limit to u and feeds THAT SAME value into its internal fractional-delay filter and command ring, so its plant model and the DAC receive identical commands. An asymmetric clamp placed after fsp would cut the command without fsp knowing -- the model would believe it sent +12.5 while the mirror got +10, which is the command-echo mismatch behind the 2026-07-16 310 Hz spiral. A downstream clamp matched EXACTLY to these bounds is fine as a backstop, never tighter.
params._clamp: SYMMETRIC +-1, and the per-axis asymmetry is gone with the 2.5 V bias that caused it (see the parport_dac _offset note). At the measured Kx=3.787 and 15.5 px per error unit, 0.27 V already sweeps the beam out of a 32x32 ROI, so +-1 is 59 px of authority against a +-16 px window -- far more than the loop needs, and small enough that a mismodelled K cannot reach a mechanical stop. Widen only after a clean run, and widen the downstream backstop clamp in the same edit.
params._start_delay: = attenuation_test start_delay(100) + open_time(500), so fsp's own hold spans the ENTIRE recorded open phase instead of closing while attenuation_test is still feeding it data it should not act on.
params._ramp: 10 s starting at t=600 lands the bumpless handover well inside attenuation_test's 120 s settle_time, so full authority is reached long before the closed-loop recording window (t=720-1220) starts.
params._guard: burst guard ON (guard_ratio 4): per-axis band-pass detector on the raw error at the regeneration freq fs/(2*(delay+delay_frac)); on a burst the axis's authority is cut to 0 for guard_hold s, learning freezes, then authority ramps back over guard_ramp s. The detector now sits at ~685 Hz (x) / ~722 Hz (y) with the 07-31 delays. Recurring activations = re-measure K/delay at the current bias; on this transport the likeliest cause is Kx, which wanders a few percent per hour (see _K_warning).

y._K: 3.646 +/- 0.011, the SMALL-SIGNAL plateau (fsm_bodey_par_small5.dat, +-20 mV, <=30 Hz, 2026-07-31 11:43), barely a change from the 3.636 PAR-1..3 ran. DO NOT copy the 3.5103 on fsm_bodey_par2.dat's fit line: that is the +-100 mV figure, and the SAME file's half-amplitude pass reads 3.662 -- y picked up ~4% of compression on 07-31 that it did not have on 07-30. Small-signal reads agree tightly across amplitude and file: 3.668 at 8 mV, 3.646 at 20 mV, 3.662 at 50 mV. Holding y fixed makes it the control for the Kx change: if PAR-4 improves x and leaves y alone, the improvement is the K fix and not the environment.
y._delay: MEASURED 2+0.577 = 2.577 fr (fsm_bodey_par.dat full-band phase slope, tau 0.4165 ms at fs 3786.38, hidden bode frame included). Was 5+0.828.
y._freqs: RE-DERIVED 2026-07-30 from attenuation_par_fsp1's own open PSD, ranked by energy in a +-1.5 Hz window with a prominence test against the local baseline. fsp.h:127 caps modes at 8/axis, so this is a budget: 5.6 and 12.0 are HUMPS not lines (prominence 2.0 and 1.9) and get zeta 0.05 to match, everything else is a genuine line. Dropped: 5.64->5.6 and 11.3->12.0 (both were off their real peaks), and the 20.0/zeta-0.3 broadband hump, whose slot went to 120.2 Hz -- a prominence-33x line carrying 0.0352 px that no config has ever modelled. Added 26.8 (0.1472 px, prominence 5.7). NOT added: 99.9 and 107.3, which prominence 1.8/1.2 says are not lines on this axis at all, just the tallest bins of the 60-150 hump. Rollback list: [5.64, 11.3, 21.1, 29.6, 57.5, 20.0].

x._clamp: The per-axis clamp override is GONE with the 2.5 V bias that required it. At offset 0 the command window is symmetric for both axes regardless of the sign of scale, so x inherits the global +-1.
x._K: 4.05 as of 2026-07-31, and now the same number at EVERY amplitude: fsm_bodex_par2.dat (12:23, +-100 mV) fits 4.0500 +/- 0.0037 with its half-amplitude pass at 4.092, and fsm_bodex_par_small7.dat (+-20 mV) fits 4.056 +/- 0.023 with its +-8 mV pass at 4.020. PAR-1..3 all ran 3.787, so they configured K ~7% LOW and OVER-commanded x by ~7% -- the direction PAR-3's own phi reconstruction pointed at (x disturbance 28% above the open-phase error, closed-window bound 0.045 px above the open-window 0.034 px, neither of which y showed). Fixing it is the one controller change in PAR-4. Note the 3.787 was NOT a large-signal artefact: the plant genuinely moved between 07-30 and 07-31, since the 100 mV pass now reads the same 4.05 the small sweeps do.
x._delay: x inherits the global 2+0.72 = 2.717 fr (fsm_bodex_par.dat, tau 0.4532 ms at fs 3788.32). Was 6+0.0.
x._freqs: RE-DERIVED 2026-07-30 from attenuation_par_fsp1's own open PSD (method as in the y _freqs note; 8-mode cap per fsp.h:127). Corrections to real peaks: 9.8->9.2, 12.0->12.9, 21.7->21.3, 57.5->57.3, 83.3->84.2. Dropped 24.9 (prominence 1.8, no line there) and the 20.0/zeta-0.3 hump. Added 18.5 (0.1048 px, prominence 4.4), 26.8 (0.0635 px, 4.9) and 120.2 (0.0382 px, prominence 40x -- the strongest unmodelled line on either axis). NOT added: 78.6, 99.9 and 143.4, genuine lines but only 0.014-0.022 px each, which lose to everything above on a fixed budget. Rollback list: [9.8, 12.0, 21.7, 24.9, 57.5, 83.3, 20.0].

pipeline._note: Backstop only, matched EXACTLY to fsp's own +-1 bounds. doc/devices/fsp.md permits a matched downstream clamp and forbids a tighter one: fsp feeds its clamped command into its own fractional-delay filter and command ring, so anything cut here would desync its plant model from what the DAC received -- the command-echo mismatch behind the 2026-07-16 310 Hz spiral. Widen this in the same edit as fsp's clamp, never separately.

Full-rate [y,x] COMMAND record, placed AFTER the clamp so it is exactly the vector parport_dac converts to volts -- command units are volts here (scale 1.0 V/unit, offset 0), so this file is directly readable as DAC volts. Deliberately complementary to the .dat attenuation_test writes, which contains only error PSDs: nothing in that file describes the command, and a PSD has no time axis. Both gaps have already cost a diagnosis on this rig -- the 2026-07-30 497 Hz limit cycle was 97.6% of the command power in a single line and near-invisible in the error, and the transient-recovery latch the same day would have read as a merely disappointing closed PSD. ~260 MB for the 1220 s run at 56 B/sample.
PARPORT DAC. TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage: ch0 = y/tip (DACA, +1.0 V/unit) = index 0, ch1 = x/tilt (DACB, -1.0 V/unit) = index 1. The fsp output is plain [y,x] in command units.
pipeline._range: 0-5 (unipolar, DACRANGE code 0x0), biased at mid-range 2.5 V so the command has 2.5 V of headroom both ways without a bipolar range. 76 uV/LSB -- 2x finer than +-5. Same range, offset and scale as conf_bode_par_x/y.json, which is REQUIRED for the measured K to transfer.
pipeline._avss_note: AVSS MUST BE -12 V here (NOT grounded), because range_max reaches +-10 and the mirror needs negative drive on an impact. SLASEH2A 7.5's footroom is 1.25 V at |load| <= 10 mA and 1.5 V at |load| <= 15 mA, so -10 V out needs AVSS <= -11.25 / -11.5 V: -12 V gives 0.75 / 0.50 V of margin, +12 V the same on AVDD for +10 V. THAT MARGIN IS THIN -- a nominal 12 V rail at -5% is 11.4 V, which fails the 15 mA case. Meter both rails UNDER LOAD.
pipeline._avss_tradeoff: ACCEPTED TRADE: with AVSS at -12 V the 0-5 base range runs OUTSIDE its characterized condition -- SLASEH2A 7.5 gives the unipolar figures (TUE +-0.07 %FSR, offset, zero-code 0.15 %FSR) at AVSS = 0 V, and the -21.5 V <= AVSS < 0 rows are the BIPOLAR ones. Unavoidable if the loop must go negative: grounding AVSS makes bipolar ranges physically impossible. The bipolar TUE at negative AVSS is actually tighter (+-0.05 %FSR), so the part is likely happy, but it is not guaranteed. Worth stating in the run notes, since it applies to the 0-5 phase this harness spends most of its time in.
pipeline._authority_check: scale 1.0 V/unit about a 0 V bias with fsp clamp +-1 => the loop commands +-1 V, which at the measured Kx=3.787 (58.7 px/V, 17 mV/px) is +-59 px against a +-15.5 px ROI. That is deliberately a small fraction of the mirror's -10..+10 V: the ROI, not the mirror, is the binding constraint on this rig, and the loop only needs ~0.1 V to hold the DC pointing offset. Command units ARE volts. The DAC range is fixed at +-5 (153 uV/LSB = 0.009 px, ~112 codes per pixel), so quantization sits ~40x below the residual.
pipeline._range_max: AUTO-RANGING, ceiling +-10 = the mirror's full range. Starts in 0-5 and widens only when the command leaves it, picking the NARROWEST range that fits: positive excursions 0-5 -> 0-6 -> 0-10 (staying unipolar, finer LSB); any NEGATIVE voltage forces bipolar, 0-5 -> +-5 -> +-6 -> +-10. See steering_par_fsp.json's _range_max_impact and _range_max_glitch.
pipeline._range_max_attenuation_warning: FOR THIS A/B HARNESS SPECIFICALLY, CONSIDER PINNING range_max TO "0-5" FOR THE MEASUREMENT RUN. Auto-ranging is now LIVE (clamp_min -12.5 reaches -10 V), so a range change CAN fire mid-run -- and when it does it injects a one-frame transient AND steps the quantization, both landing in the closed-loop RMS you are trying to measure. Worse, it would fire only in the CLOSED phase, not the open one, biasing exactly the comparison this harness exists to make. Two clean options: (a) pin range_max to "0-5" so the range is fixed for the whole run and the number is directly comparable to attenuation_fsp15/21, or (b) leave it live to characterise real operational behaviour, and report the range-change count alongside the RMS so the reader knows the actuator was not a fixed-gain element. Do not quietly do (b) and present it as (a).
pipeline._scale_sign: y positive, x negative -- same signs as the piplate config (+2/-2), halved in magnitude. The sign belongs to the optical/mechanical path, not the converter.
pipeline._sync_update: left OFF. With two driven channels the async skew is one frame, ~6.4 us -- ~2% of the 264 us loop period and below the platform's own ~6.8 us SCHED_FIFO / ~32 us C-state jitter. Turn it on only if axis cross-coupling appears that tracks scheduling hiccups rather than the command; see doc/devices/parport_dac.md, Update mode.

params._offset: 0, NOT the 2.5 V bias this file was written around. K and the delay were both measured at offset 0 (mirror parked at 0 V) in conf_bode_par_x/y.json, and K is bias-dependent -- running the loop at a different operating point than the bode would invalidate the very numbers this harness reports. Command units are volts about 0, so the command bounds are symmetric and the per-axis asymmetry is gone.
params._range: +-5 to match the bode sweeps exactly. 153 uV/LSB instead of the 76 uV/LSB the 0-5 unipolar range gave, which is the price of running symmetric about 0 -- still 6.5x finer than the BRIDGEplate's 12-bit 1 mV.
params._range_max: REMOVED. With the command bounded at +-1 V the DAC can never leave the +-5 base range, so auto-ranging is dead code here -- parport_dac would log a warning saying exactly that at init. It also settles the _range_max_attenuation_warning below in favour of option (a): the range is fixed for the whole run, so the open and closed phases see an identical fixed-gain actuator and the RMS comparison is clean. Restore it only together with a wider clamp.
params._verify: off in the closed loop: verify turns each write into 3 frames plus a non-posted status read per bit. Exercise it with conf_parport_dac_smoke.json before the run, not during it.
params._skip_unchanged: OFF. It skips very little anyway at 153 uV/LSB (a live command changes the code almost every iteration), and a write is 6.4 us against a 264 us period, so it buys nothing measurable. Off also means the DAC register is refreshed every frame instead of being written once and left, which is the more robust state on this wiring.
